edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant responds to Plaintiff's First Requests for Production subject to the general and specific objections set forth herein. Defendant's responses are based on information reasonably available at this time and are made without waiver of any objection, privilege, protection, or right to supplement.

1. GENERAL OBJECTIONS. Defendant objects to each request to the extent it seeks information or documents protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, common-interest doctrine, or any other applicable privilege or protection; seeks documents not relevant to any claim or defense; is not proportional to the needs of the case; is overbroad, unduly burdensome, or duplicative; or seeks documents outside Defendant's possession, custody, or control.

2. PRODUCTION. Subject to and without waiving the foregoing objections, Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents within its possession, custody, or control following a reasonable search and collection process.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. To the extent Defendant withholds responsive documents on the basis of privilege or work-product protection, Defendant will identify such documents on a privilege log consistent with the applicable rules and any governing order of the Court.
4. RESERVATION. Defendant reserves all rights, objections, privileges, and protections, including the right to amend, supplement, or correct these responses as discovery proceeds.

edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant responds to Plaintiff's First Requests for Production based on information reasonably available after a reasonable inquiry. These responses are made subject to the specific objections and responses stated for each request. Defendant does not rely on any general objection to withhold documents unless that objection is expressly stated in response to a particular request and the response states that responsive documents are being withheld on that basis. Defendant reserves the right to supplement or amend these responses as discovery proceeds.
edits.name: Revised Preliminary Statement

edits.text: 1. GENERAL OBJECTIONS. Defendant objects to the Requests to the extent they seek documents protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, common-interest doctrine, or other applicable privilege or protection; seek documents outside Defendant's possession, custody, or control; impose obligations beyond those required by the applicable rules or any Court order; or seek documents whose collection and production would be disproportionate to the needs of the case. These General Objections are incorporated into the specific responses only where expressly referenced, and no documents are being withheld based solely on these General Objections absent an express statement in an individual response.
edits.name: Narrowed General Objections

edits.text: 2. SEARCH, CUSTODIANS, DATE RANGE, AND PRODUCTION TIMING. Subject to the specific responses below, Defendant will conduct a reasonable search for responsive, non-privileged documents within its possession, custody, or control. Defendant's initial collection will include the following custodians likely to possess responsive documents: the Executive's direct manager, the Human Resources business partner assigned to the Executive's business unit, the employee-relations representative involved in the events at issue, and the in-house counsel custodian for non-privileged business communications, as appropriate. Defendant's initial date range for collection is January 1 of the year preceding the events alleged in the Complaint through the date the Complaint was filed, unless a different date range is stated in an individual response or agreed by the parties. Defendant will begin producing responsive, non-privileged documents on a rolling basis within 30 days of service of these amended responses and will substantially complete its initial production within 60 days, subject to reasonable adjustments for volume, privilege review, ESI processing, and any agreed search protocol.
edits.name: Search and Production Details

edits.text: 3. PRIVILEGE LOG. To the extent Defendant withholds responsive documents on the basis of attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, common-interest protection, or any other applicable privilege or protection, Defendant will identify such documents on a privilege log consistent with the applicable rules and any governing Court order. Defendant will not log communications or work product created after commencement of this litigation unless required by Court order or agreement of the parties. Defendant will provide its privilege log within a reasonable time after substantial completion of its initial production.
edits.name: Revised Privilege Log Provision

edits.text: 4. INDIVIDUAL RESPONSES. Defendant will answer each Request for Production individually. For each request, Defendant will state: (a) the specific objections, if any; (b) whether responsive documents are being withheld on the basis of any objection; (c) the scope of the search and production for that request, including any limitation by custodian, source, date range, or subject matter; and (d) whether Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents. Where Defendant agrees to produce documents, production will be made in accordance with Section 2 above unless otherwise stated in the individual response.
edits.name: Individual Response Requirement

edits.text: 5. FORM OF INDIVIDUAL RESPONSE. For each numbered request, Defendant's response will use the following format: 'Response to Request No. __: Defendant objects to this Request to the extent [state specific objection(s)]. Subject to and without waiving those objections, Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents located after a reasonable search of [identify custodians/sources] for the period [identify date range]. Defendant is withholding documents on the basis of the stated objections [yes/no; if yes, identify category withheld]. Privileged documents, if any, will be logged in accordance with Section 3.'
edits.name: Template for Specific RFP Responses

edits.text: 6. RESERVATION. Defendant reserves all rights, objections, privileges, and protections, including the right to amend, supplement, or correct these responses based on additional information, party agreement, Court order, or further developments in discovery. Nothing in these responses shall be construed as an admission that any requested documents exist, are relevant, are admissible, or are within Defendant's possession, custody, or control.
edits.name: Revised Reservation
